San Francisco Oracle, vol. 1 no. 10, cover

The front page of the Haight-Ashbury underground newspaper, October 1967: a mandala of rings and checkerboards in magenta, violet, and turquoise on newsprint.

Source
Internet Archive: San Francisco Oracle Vol. 1 No. 10 (Daniel D. Teoli Jr. Archival Collection)
Creator
The Oracle of the City of San Francisco (Allen Cohen, editor); cover artist not identified
Made
October 1967
Style
Psychedelic art (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Hallucinatory, dense, countercultural
Evidence
Downloaded page 1 of the Teoli scan (2704 × 4073 px) to a scratch folder and inspected it. The cover is signed at lower center with a name I could not read, dated ’67. The Letterform Archive scans of other issues on Internet Archive are stream-only. The image is not stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The Oracle was an underground newspaper published in 12 issues from September 1966 to February 1968 in the Haight-Ashbury, edited by Allen Cohen with Michael Bowen as art director. Wikipedia calls it “arguably the outstanding example of psychedelia” in the underground press. Wikipedia.

From issue 6 the paper was printed at Howard Quinn Printers, where its artists perfected the split-fountain rainbow effect by damming the ink fountain to feed several colors at once. The print run peaked at about 125,000. Wikipedia.

The Internet Archive item states a CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 license from the scanning collector. That license covers the scan, not the 1967 artwork.

Observed

  • ORACLE fills an arch across the top in fat turquoise letters with violet shadows and outlines. THE CITY OF SAN FRANCISCO curves above it in smaller letters.
  • A large mandala of concentric rings, lobes, and interlocking circles fills the middle. Its center is a small target of tight rings.
  • Warped checkerboards in magenta, violet, turquoise, and paper color fill every corner and recede like a tunnel.
  • An embracing couple drawn in rough outline stands at the bottom center, under a figure-eight sign.
  • The inks are magenta, violet, and turquoise on yellowed newsprint. Prices, the date, and the issue number are lettered by hand into the pattern.

Why it belongs

This page meets all four diagnostics of the rubric: complementary colors side by side, a swollen masthead, a symmetrical central medallion, and rings and patterns that fill the background.

Low-cost three-ink newsprint produced the same effect as the poster work, which suggests the look depends on arrangement more than on premium printing.

Borrow

Arch a fat masthead over a central mandala and let pattern fill the rest.

Use a warped checkerboard that recedes toward the center to give depth without shading.

Letter small facts, such as price and date, into the pattern instead of into a separate box.
